partner_results_applied.use: Exact bathtub/product-set reduction; translates the fixed-A density theorem to the product-shell-volume form.
Complementary continuous-density cross-block theorem; used to frame the remaining local-versus-delocalized quantitative bridge.

claims: For any absolutely continuous input vector and nonzero real symmetric A, X^T A X is absolutely continuous.
For independent four-coordinate inputs of densities <=1 and invertible symmetric B, the affine quadratic density is bounded by (4*pi+8)/sigma_min(B).
Every real symmetric matrix of rank >=3 has a nonsingular principal submatrix of order 3 or 4.

Consequently every fixed real symmetric A of rank >=3 and every allowed independent input law give an essentially bounded density, with an explicit finite matrix-dependent principal-pivot certificate.

unresolved_implication: Obtain a dimension-free aggregate-curvature payment replacing the matrix-dependent reciprocal principal-pivot scale; a candidate next step is a uniform principal-block versus rank-three cross-block dichotomy that retains all additional spectral terms.
next_step: Attack the local/cross-block dichotomy on mixed-leverage rank-three and higher-rank matrices; either prove universal constants or construct a source-valid matrix family where both resources are simultaneously small.
